faqs.q: How often is general pest control serviced?

faqs.q: Do you treat inside the home?
faqs.a: Yes. Every general pest control visit includes interior treatment of baseboards, cracks, crevices, and problem areas, along with exterior foundation and yard treatment.

faqs.q: Is general pest control safe for kids and pets?
faqs.a: Yes. We use EPA-approved products applied by licensed technicians. Treated areas are safe once dry, and we give you specific guidance for every visit.

faqs.q: Why do fleas keep coming back after I treat my pet?
faqs.a: Most of the flea population lives in the environment as eggs and larvae, not on your pet. Treating the yard and home breaks the life cycle so fleas stop returning.

faqs.q: Where do ticks live in my yard?
faqs.a: Ticks live in wooded edges, tall grass, leaf litter, and shaded, humid areas. Those zones are the focus of every tick treatment.

faqs.q: Is flea and tick treatment safe for my pets?
faqs.a: Yes. Treatments use EPA-approved products, and pets can return to treated areas once they are dry.

headline: Rodent Control That Gets Mice and Rats Out for Good
intro: Selke Pest Control's rodent control removes mice and rats from homes across Lake Norman and the Charlotte Metro. It starts with a full inspection of the attic, crawl space, garage, and exterior to find activity and entry points, followed by targeted trapping, tamper-resistant bait stations, and monitoring visits until activity stops. Pair it with exclusion work to keep rodents from getting back in.
frequency: Initial service plus monitoring visits until activity stops

included.title: Full inspection
included.desc: Attic, crawl space, garage, and exterior checked for droppings, rub marks, and entry points.

included.title: Trapping
included.desc: Traps placed along the paths rodents travel inside the home.

included.title: Tamper-resistant bait stations
included.desc: Exterior stations that reduce rodent pressure while keeping pets and children safe.

included.title: Monitoring visits
included.desc: Return visits check traps and stations until activity is gone.

faqs.q: How do I know if I have mice or rats?
faqs.a: Common signs include scratching in walls or the attic at night, droppings in cabinets or the garage, chewed packaging, and grease marks along walls.

faqs.q: How small of a gap can a mouse fit through?
faqs.a: A mouse can squeeze through a gap about the size of a dime. That is why sealing entry points with exclusion work is important after rodents are removed.

faqs.q: When are rodents most active in the Charlotte area?
faqs.a: Rodent activity rises from September through February as mice and rats move indoors looking for warmth and food.

name: Exclusion Work
summary: Seal the gaps, vents, and openings pests use to get inside, so rodents and insects stay out for good.
metaTitle: Pest Exclusion Services in Charlotte & Lake Norman, NC | Selke Pest Control
metaDescription: Pest exclusion for Lake Norman and Charlotte Metro homes. We seal gaps, vents, and entry points with durable materials to keep rodents and insects out.
headline: Exclusion Work That Keeps Pests From Getting Back In
intro: Exclusion is the physical work of sealing the openings pests use to enter a home. Selke Pest Control inspects the foundation, rooflines, vents, garage doors, and utility penetrations, then seals gaps with durable, rodent-resistant materials such as copper mesh, hardware cloth, sealant, door sweeps, and vent screens. Exclusion pairs with rodent control and general pest control for long-term protection.
frequency: One-time project, with a follow-up check

included.title: Entry-point inspection
included.desc: Foundation, rooflines, soffits, vents, and garage doors checked for openings.

included.title: Gap sealing
included.desc: Holes and gaps closed with copper mesh, hardware cloth, and exterior-grade sealant.

included.title: Door sweeps & garage seals
included.desc: Gaps under doors and garage doors closed where pests slip in.

included.title: Vent & utility screening
included.desc: Crawl space vents, dryer vents, and pipe penetrations screened and sealed.

faqs.a: Exclusion is sealing the gaps, cracks, vents, and openings pests use to get inside, so they are physically blocked from entering your home.

faqs.q: Do I need exclusion if I already have pest control?
faqs.a: Treatments reduce pests, while exclusion removes the way in. Homes with rodent activity or recurring invaders get the best long-term results with both.
We use durable, rodent-resistant materials such as copper mesh, hardware cloth, exterior-grade sealant, door sweeps, and vent screens.

included.title: Carpenter ant treatment

included.title: Carpenter bee treatment
included.desc: Active galleries in decks, fascia, and eaves treated in spring.

included.title: Prevention advice
included.desc: Guidance on sealing holes, painting bare wood, and fixing moisture problems.

faqs.a: No. Carpenter ants tunnel through damp or damaged wood to build nests, which can weaken it over time. Finding the moisture source is part of treatment.

faqs.q: When are carpenter bees most active?
faqs.a: Carpenter bees are most active in spring, when they drill new galleries in bare or weathered wood such as decks, fascia, and eaves.

faqs.q: How do you treat fire ants in a lawn?
faqs.a: We treat active mounds directly and apply a broadcast lawn treatment so new colonies are less likely to form.
